title: Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings
summary: Due to the availability of powerful analytic techniques, vastly superior lower bounds are known for the measurable chromatic number of Euclidean spaces compared to their ordinary chromatic number. Indeed, even the breakthrough lower bound of 5 for the famous Hadwiger-Nelson problem lagged over 35 years behind that of the measurable setting. This raises the fundamental question of whether the measurable and ordinary chromatic number of Euclidean spaces differ as conjectured by Székely in 1984.
